rationale: The golden submission is graded against a hidden ground_truth.json that was derived from a different, inconsistent netlist definition than the one actually shipped in inputs/locked_netlist.v. Two structural mismatches are visible in the provided files: (1) instance naming — inputs/locked_netlist.v names its lock instances u_keymux0..u_keymux3, while the private ground_truth/locked_netlist.v (used to derive the golden answer) names them keymux_N10_lock/keymux_N11_lock/keymux_N16_lock/keymux_N19_lock — completely disjoint identifiers, which alone explains SR1's F1=0.000 with missing=4/extra=4. (2) mux select polarity — inputs/locked_netlist.v implements Y=(S&B)|(~S&A) (S=1 selects B, S=0 selects A), but the private ground_truth mux2x1 module implements Y=(A&S)|(B&~S) (S=1 selects A, S=0 selects B), i.e. the opposite polarity. This flips the correct resolved_value at 3 of the 4 loci, matching the observed key_recovery_rate=0.250 with mismatched indices [0,2,3]. This is not an evaluator logic bug — it is a genuine inconsistency between the shipped participant-facing netlist and the private ground-truth artifacts used to build the golden answer and evaluate.py's hidden ground truth.
revision_instructions: Regenerate the private ground-truth artifacts (evaluation/private/ground_truth.json, golden/recovered_key.json, and any ground_truth/*.v reference files) by tracing the SAME netlist shipped at inputs/locked_netlist.v — do not use a separately authored mux2x1/instance-naming scheme. Concretely: (1) instance names in ground_truth.json and the golden key_gates array must exactly match the instance names actually present in inputs/locked_netlist.v (currently u_keymux0, u_keymux1, u_keymux2, u_keymux3), found by grep for 'keymux'. (2) The resolved_value semantics must be derived from the actual mux expression used in inputs/locked_netlist.v: Y = (S & B) | (~S & A), meaning S=0 selects A and S=1 selects B — do not reuse a different polarity convention. Re-derive the correct key bit at each of the 4 loci by determining, from the original (unlocked) c17-like reference circuit, whether input A or input B at each keymux reproduces the correct signal, and set resolved_value accordingly under this polarity. Then regenerate the golden submission/key file so it is internally consistent with this corrected ground truth, and rerun the differential test to confirm golden_run now passes and vulnerable_run still fails.
